rubrics.justification: It reasonably notes an expanded blastocyst and difficulty assessing ICM/TE, but it overcalls 'multiple large vacuoles' and builds much of the assessment on a likely fabricated or at least highly uncertain image feature not reliably supported by the image alone.

It integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, sperm parameters, endometrium, diagnosis, and lifestyle factors with prognosis in a generally thoughtful way, though some links to embryo morphology are overstated.

The structure is logical, but the probability estimate and major conclusions are heavily driven by speculative vacuolization and somewhat aggressive penalty stacking, which weakens the support for the final prognosis.

Much is broadly consistent with IVF practice, but recommending freeze-all for this case, low-dose aspirin, ERA after a first failure, and PGT-A in a 32-year-old after one failed cycle are not strongly guideline-based; citing Istanbul consensus for this abnormality is also questionable.
It provides clear next steps for transfer counseling, lifestyle modification, and follow-up, though some recommendations are more speculative than standard-of-care.
